output.brief: The longer SME approval times are mainly caused by the valuation stage for property-secured loans, not by staff, Corvane, or the valuation firm. Since the Credit Policy v14 change on 2 May, loans between $150k and $500k must have a full appraisal instead of a desktop valuation. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the same firm whose turnaround has not changed, so the valuation stage rose from about 1.7 to 8 days. Unsecured loans, consumer loans on the same system, and underwriting times are essentially unchanged. The headline withdrawal rise is partly an artifact: 32 of the 73 closures since May were automatic 30-day closures for missing document uploads. Next steps: ask the credit risk committee to review the valuation requirement with the measured delay, and add a stage-by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Hold off on performance plans for new hires, the Corvane payment decision, and fee rebates. Confidence is moderate, because I did not check the policy's risk rationale or the June timing of the valuation jump.
